We need to step up the work around establishing a clear shared understanding of which parts of Ethereum are guaranteed & won’t change, and which are closer to “implementation specifics” that may or may not change in the future, and reliance on them is at ones own risk. Today, this distinction is very fuzzy.

01:25:06	Jango:	Replying to "appreciate it"

not impractical, but lossy. try/catch feels most natural: one bad recipient shouldn't block a batch or lock a withdrawal, so you catch and move on. the higher-level alternatives all exist and all cost something: pull payments / retry queues (a new slot per failure, 110k under glam, plus a second tx someone has to know to send), check-before-call (only works if you control the callee, which in an open system we usually dont), or a gas pre-check before the call (needs a gasReq constant, which I agree hard coding gas stuff is not beautiful code).
